question: Can strictly OOS condition-adjusted expected-performance residual states break the L1 top1 podium ceiling?

variants.RESIDUAL_V1: V1 lag/state + simple network expectation residuals
variants.V2_FINISH_RESIDUAL: V1 raw lag/state + OOS expected finish-percentile residual state
variants.V2_MULTI_RESIDUAL: V1 raw lag/state + OOS finish/speed/last3f residual states
variants.HYBRID_V1_V2_MULTI: V1 residual state + all V2 OOS residual states

v2_expectation.features: STRUCTURAL pre-race L1 features only; no odds/popularity
v2_expectation.training: For race year Y, expectation models use only Y-1 for 2020 or Y-2,Y-1 for 2021-2025.
v2_expectation.2019: No V2 expectation residual because no earlier snapshot year is available.
v2_expectation.same_day_duplicates: Never ordered within day; duplicate OOS residuals are averaged only for future-date state updates.

strictness: Every V2 expectation is out-of-sample by calendar year.
Every residual state feature is shifted by at least one horse race date.
Current-race outcome never enters its own features.
Final L1 walk-forward remains two prior years -> next unknown year, 2021-2025.
No odds or popularity are used.
promotion_rule: Require >=2.0pp pooled top1_top3 uplift and no fold worse than -0.5pp.
